name: heatsink_forced_mlp
description: PINNeAPPle ModelRegistry 'bench_mlp' (4 x 128, SiLU) on log-scaled geometry, material and operating variables, trained on 6000 solves of the HeatSink Sizer physics engine (Teertstra composite parallel-plate model, 3-D finite-volume base conduction, developing-flow pressure drop). Returns the resistance, the pressure drop and a split-conformal 95 % upper bound on the resistance.
task: Plate-fin heat sink in ducted forced convection: base-to-air thermal resistance and pressure drop

outputs.name: r_base_k_w
outputs.description: thermal resistance, base to ambient air

validity_range.fin_gap_note: gap sampled in 0.8-10 mm, then the fin count is rounded; the realised gaps of the training designs span 0.56-12.2 mm
validity_range.regime: ducted (no bypass) laminar/developing forced convection in air

known_limitations: Ducted flow: real heat sinks with bypass lose 20-50 % of the airflow; correct the velocity first.
Convection correlations carry a typical +-15 % accuracy; the surrogate's own error (<1 % mean) is against the engine, not against a measurement.
Screening tool: re-verify a chosen design with the physics engine.
equations: Teertstra, Yovanovich & Culham (2000) composite parallel-plate Nusselt number
3-D finite-volume conduction in the base (spreading resistance)
developing-flow friction + entry/exit losses for the pressure drop

training_config.optimizer: Adam (Trainer, best-val checkpoint, 400 epochs, lr 2e-3) + L-BFGS polish

reference_source: 900 held-out designs solved by the HeatSink Sizer physics engine (pinneapple_design.thermal.heatsink.engine). The engine is checked against independent methods: Lee et al. spreading (1-5 %), Stephan developing-flow Nu + e-NTU (0-5 %), fully developed friction (2-4 %), FVM grid convergence < 2 %.
citation: PINNeAPPle contributors (2026). HeatSink Sizer forced-convection surrogate. PINNeAPPle model zoo, https://github.com/PINNeAPPle-Labs/PINNeAPPle

monotonic: more airflow never raises the resistance (share of held-out designs violating, +5 % step)
monotonic: a more conductive material never raises the resistance (share of held-out designs violating, +5 % step)
monotonic: a wider heat source spreads less (lower resistance) (share of held-out designs violating, +5 % step)
monotonic: pressure drop grows with air velocity (share of held-out designs violating, +5 % step)
R > 0 and dP > 0 on the held-out designs
